en.name: Cotija
en.summary: Cotija in its proper aged form — Cotija de Montaña, the añejo style — is dry, hard and heavily salted, a grating cheese that keeps like a parmesan. Refrigerated it runs about 3–6 months, and it freezes for about 6 months. If yours is wet and crumbles like feta, it is a fresh cheese and this record does not apply.
en.pantry: An aged cotija is salty and dry enough to survive an afternoon on the counter, but it is still a cheese and the cupboard is not where it lives. Warmth makes it sweat fat and softens the dry crumb that makes it useful. Grate what you need and put the block straight back. A moist supermarket cotija is a different matter and must not be left out at all — treat it as a fresh cheese and follow the 2-hour rule, 1 hour above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: Wrap it in waxed or greaseproof paper inside a loose bag — sealed plastic makes it sweat — and keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. A working range of 3–6 months is reasonable for a hard block, borrowed from what is published for hard cheese rather than measured on cotija: an unopened piece sits at the long end and a wedge you have been cutting into for weeks sits at the short end. Surface mould on a hard cheese can be cut a good inch away and the rest used.
en.freezer: Cotija freezes for about 6 months at −18 °C (0 °F), again a hard-cheese figure applied here rather than a published cotija one. Freezing makes a hard cheese crumbly, which barely matters for something you were going to grate anyway. Freeze it in a block rather than grated, double-wrapped, and grate it from part-frozen straight onto the food. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are about quality.
en.thawing: Grate it straight from part-frozen, or thaw it wrapped in the fridge. Never thaw cheese on the counter, and do not refreeze it.
spoilage: Fuzzy growth spreading into the paste rather than sitting on the surface.
A rancid, crayon-like smell from the fat.
A slimy or wet surface on what should be a dry block.
Deep discolouration, or a bitter taste.
tips: Buy a block rather than a tub of pre-crumbled cheese; it keeps far longer.
Waxed paper and a loose bag, never an airtight plastic box.
Grate only what you are about to use.
Check which cotija you have: dry and hard, or wet and fresh — they store differently.

faq.q: How long does cotija keep in the fridge?
faq.a: Treat an aged, dry block as a hard cheese: roughly 3–6 months at 4 °C or below, with a wedge you have been cutting into at the short end.
Yes, about 6 months at −18 °C. Freeze it as a block and grate from part-frozen; it comes out crumblier, which does not matter for grating.
No. The aged mountain style is rock hard and long-keeping. Much of what is sold as cotija abroad is a moist fresh cheese closer to queso fresco, which is far more perishable.

faq.q: Can you cut mould off cotija?
faq.a: On a genuinely hard, dry block you can cut well clear of the spot and use the rest. On a moist, crumbly one, discard it.

zh.name: 科蒂哈乳酪
zh.summary: 真正陳年的科蒂哈——山區的 Cotija de Montaña、也就是 añejo 型——乾硬鹹重，是一種像帕瑪森那樣的刨絲乳酪。冷藏大約 3～6 個月，冷凍大約 6 個月。如果你買到的是濕潤、像費塔一樣散開的那種，那是新鮮乳酪，不適用這一篇。
zh.pantry: 陳年科蒂哈夠鹹夠乾，在室溫下擺一個下午不至於出事，但它終究是乳酪，櫥櫃不是它的住處。溫度一高就會滲油，也會讓那種乾鬆的質地變軟，而那正是它好用的原因。刨下要用的量，整塊立刻冰回去。超市賣的濕潤款則完全不同，根本不能放室溫——請當新鮮乳酪處理，遵守 2 小時原則，超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。
zh.fridge: 用蠟紙或防油紙包好，再套一個不密封的袋子——密封塑膠會讓它出汗——放在 4 °C 以下。硬塊可以比照硬質乳酪的公告值，把 3～6 個月當成合理區間，而不是科蒂哈自己的實測數字：未開封的整塊接近長的那一端，已經切了好幾週的楔形塊則接近短的那一端。硬質乳酪表面長霉，可以連周圍兩三公分一起切掉，其餘照用。
zh.freezer: 科蒂哈在 −18 °C 下大約可放 6 個月，同樣是硬質乳酪的數字借用過來，不是科蒂哈的公告值。冷凍會讓硬質乳酪變碎，但反正你本來就要刨絲，影響不大。整塊冷凍不要先刨，包兩層，之後半解凍狀態下直接刨到菜上。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數講的是品質。
zh.thawing: 半解凍狀態直接刨用，或連包裝放冷藏解凍。乳酪不要放室溫解凍，也不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 絨毛狀的霉不只在表面，而是往內部蔓延。
脂肪產生油耗味、蠟筆味。
本該乾燥的塊體表面變得濕黏。
顏色深層變化，或吃起來發苦。
tips: 買整塊而不是已經弄碎的盒裝，耐放很多。
蠟紙包、鬆口袋裝，絕對不要密封塑膠盒。
先確認手上是哪一種：乾硬型還是濕潤新鮮型，保存方式完全不同。

faq.q: 科蒂哈乳酪冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 乾硬的陳年塊請比照硬質乳酪：4 °C 以下大約 3～6 個月，已經切用一陣子的接近短的那一端。
可以，−18 °C 下約 6 個月。整塊冷凍、半解凍刨絲；質地會變碎，但刨絲用不受影響。

faq.q: 所有的科蒂哈都一樣嗎？
faq.a: 不一樣。山區陳年款硬如石頭、非常耐放；國外賣的很多其實是接近 queso fresco 的濕潤新鮮乳酪，容易壞得多。

faq.q: 科蒂哈長霉可以切掉嗎？
faq.a: 真正乾硬的塊體可以連周圍一起切掉再用。濕潤易碎的那種請整份丟棄。
